$comment: Handoff record for the next team or agent picking up this repository. Update the `updated` field and the relevant sections whenever the project changes materially.
updatedBy: Claude Opus 5 (agent-assisted session), reviewed by Jay W. Snyder

project.name: SIGNAL
project.description: The interactive, gamified portfolio and resume of Jay W. Snyder. A hand-written Three.js rail shooter: six sectors down a neon corridor, each one a chapter of the resume sealed behind an encryption node. Fly the corridor, clear the resistance, break the node, read the dossier it was holding, continue. Ships with an equivalent written brief for accessibility, SEO, phones and visitors in a hurry.
project.audience: Business owners and operators evaluating whether to hire Jay to build AI systems for them. Secondary: recruiters and engineering leads.
project.goal: Convert. The site is the proof that Jay builds ambitious interactive software; the written brief is the escape hatch for anyone who just wants the facts.

owner.name: Jay W. Snyder
currentRoles: Director of Sales, Marketing & Technology, SkyRun Daytona Vacation Rentals

status: v3 merged to main, plus a follow-up session that fixed the replay loop. The run now stops at every sector — including sectors already decrypted, which it used to fly straight past without showing a word of the resume — and there is a real "fly it again" that keeps every shard, rank and award. That session also found the completion card had been shipping entirely unstyled: the stylesheet was renamed from `.done` to `.finale` at the block only, so every element rule still said `.done__*` while the markup said `.finale__*`, and the card rendered 1400x1624px in a 900px viewport with all four calls to action below the fold. Vercel redeploys automatically on push to main; GitHub Pages does NOT and needs `npm run deploy` or the mirror keeps serving an older build from an indexed URL.

config.note: vercel.json intentionally makes the build explicit rather than relying on Vercel's framework auto-detection, because this project's Vercel dashboard settings were configured for the previous React/CRA-era app and may not match. Dashboard settings are overridden by vercel.json.

githubPages.verificationMethod: All five deployed artifacts fetched from the live origin returned 200 with correct content types, and their SHA-256 hashes match the local `npm run build` output byte for byte. Those live bytes were then executed in headless Chromium: engine boots, ORIGIN dossier opens on arrival, terminal responds, brief mode toggles and scrolls. The sandbox relay resets Chromium's TLS tunnel to github.io, so the browser pass ran against a byte-identical local mirror of the live files rather than the origin directly.
githubPages.knownNonIssue: Google Fonts is blocked in the build sandbox, so verification runs show one failed request for fonts.googleapis.com. Real visitors load it normally; the design falls back to system stacks if it ever fails.
githubPages.role: Mirror, not canonical. Serves identical bytes; index.html points canonical at the Vercel URL, which is exactly what canonical is for. Republish with `npm run deploy` whenever main changes, or retire it — nothing depends on it.

deployment.verificationMethod: All five deployed artifacts fetched from the live Vercel origin hash-match the local `npm run build` output byte for byte. Response headers confirm vercel.json is in effect: hashed assets return `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, neither of which Vercel adds by default. The HTML served by Vercel and by GitHub Pages is byte-identical.
deployment.browserVerification: The deployed bundle was executed in headless Chromium: engine boots, ORIGIN dossier opens on arrival, terminal responds, brief mode toggles and scrolls. The sandbox relay resets Chromium's TLS tunnel to external hosts, so the browser pass ran against a byte-identical local mirror of the live files rather than the origin directly.

stack.rendering: Three.js r180, hand-written engine (no React, no react-three-fiber)
stack.styling: Plain CSS with custom-property design tokens (no Tailwind)

bundleSize.note: Run `npm run build` for current figures. Three is split into its own chunk via rollupOptions.manualChunks so app changes do not invalidate it, and SMAAPass is a lazy dynamic import because its lookup textures are ~38 kB gzipped and only the top quality tier uses it.

commands.note: `npm run build` runs `tsc --noEmit` first, so a type error fails the build. `npm run smoke` drives the built site in headless Chromium; serve dist first with `npm run smoke:serve`. Set SKIP_PASSIVE=1 to skip the slow passive-visitor check, and CHROMIUM_PATH if Playwright cannot find a browser. Playwright and http-server are now real devDependencies — `npm run smoke` used to fail on a fresh clone because neither was declared.

architecture.loop: Fixed-step simulation at 60 Hz with an accumulator and a 5-step cap, decoupled from rendering. Frame rate never changes flight feel, weapon cadence or collision.

directories.src/core: Engine (renderer, post chain, adaptive quality tiers), Input, Audio, Events bus, Save, Math helpers
directories.src/shaders: Fresnel hull material with in-shader fog and procedural panel lines; the composite post pass
directories.src/fx: Pooled GPU particles, shockwave/flash impacts, camera-facing ribbon trails
directories.src/world: Route (the flight spline), Sector nodes, Landmarks, Corridor gates, Causeway floor, Environment props, Nebula, Starfield, Labels
directories.src/player: Rail flight model and the chase camera rig
directories.src/game: GameState (XP, ranks, shards, achievements), Combat, Pickups, Mission director
directories.src/ui: HUD, Codex dossier, Terminal, Toasts, Boot, TopBar, Brief, MissionCard, Overlay, TouchControls, Complete
directories.src/data: ALL CONTENT. Nothing user-visible is hard-coded elsewhere.
directories.scripts: smoke.mjs — behavioural regression checks, one per bug that actually shipped

notableTechniques: The route is an arc-length-parameterised spline. Forward motion is automatic and monotonic; steering only moves the ship inside a tube around the centreline, so a visitor cannot get lost or fly out of the content.

The mission director runs the same five beats six times — travel, waves, node, dossier, continue — so there is exactly one objective at any moment and the HUD always names it. Every entry into that script (launch, resume, Continue, a route-spine jump, a replay, a progress wipe) goes through one `beginSector` so they cannot drift apart, and every sector ends in a dossier: a node that is already open is handed back rather than flown past.

Stall assist: if a fight stops progressing the interface escalates, first an instruction, then automatic fire, then an explicit offer to open the dossier anyway. Nobody is locked out of a resume for being bad at a game.
The player cannot lose. Hits cost hull integrity, which regenerates.
Fresnel hull shader with FogExp2 implemented in-shader (custom ShaderMaterials do not get three fog for free) and triplanar procedural panel lines.
Causeway: a ribbon swept along the route spline, ruled with a grid, giving the corridor a floor and a vanishing point.
Adaptive quality governor steps pixel ratio, bloom, particle budget and prop density down a tier rather than stuttering. SMAA on the top tier is lazily imported.
Composite post pass driven by gameplay: boost streaks, damage vignette, explosion punch.
Procedural WebAudio throughout, including filtered noise bursts for explosions. Zero audio files ship.
architecture.debugging: `window.SIGNAL.debug()` returns distance along the route, offset, speed, barrier, hull, mission phase, objective, hostiles, particle count, quality tier and per-node state. `window.SIGNAL.goto(<sectorId>)` jumps to a sector; `window.SIGNAL.restart()` flies the corridor again from ORIGIN keeping progress; `window.SIGNAL.forceDossier()` opens the current dossier without fighting for it. `?tier=0|1|2` pins the quality tier.

content.note: src/data feeds BOTH the 3D dossiers and the written brief. Editing one updates both; they cannot drift.

files.src/data/profile.ts: Name, contact, tagline, pitch paragraphs, values, headline stats
files.src/data/content.ts: Ventures, projects, career timeline, education, services, skill groups
files.src/data/sectors.ts: How that content is laid out across the six sectors: position, colour, shard count, blocks, locked bonus block

content.howToAddAProject: Add an entry to `projects` in src/data/content.ts, then reference its id from a sector's `cards` block in src/data/sectors.ts. The written brief picks it up automatically. Encounter pacing lives separately in src/data/missions.ts.

accessibility.briefMode: Every word in the 3D world also exists as a semantic, keyboard-navigable HTML document. Toggle with the toolbar button, the `B` key, the terminal `brief` command, or the skip link.
automaticFallbacks: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> brief mode on first visit
No WebGL support -> brief mode, with an explanatory note
Any exception during engine start -> brief mode
accessibility.skipLink: First tab stop on the page, jumps to the brief and switches modes.
accessibility.liveRegion: Achievement toasts are mirrored into a polite aria-live region.
accessibility.note: The brief lives in normal document flow as a direct child of <body>, NOT inside the fixed #ui overlay. Moving it back inside #ui breaks document scrolling and in-page anchors.

seo.canonicalUrlNote: canonical, og:url, og:image and twitter:image all point at the Vercel production URL, and the JSON-LD Person `url` matches. GitHub Pages serves the same bytes as a mirror. If the site moves to a custom domain, update all five plus this field.
seo.structuredData: JSON-LD Person schema in index.html, with sameAs covering GitHub, LinkedIn and Dazzle Divas.

designDecisions.decision: Dual mode: playable world plus written brief
designDecisions.why: A client evaluating Jay at 11pm may not want to fly a spaceship. The brief protects the conversion goal and covers accessibility, SEO and low-power devices.
Matches where Jay's recent work actually is (KnotzHardDrivin and KnotzGalaga2 are both raw three + Vite + TypeScript) and shows engine-level capability that React would hide.

designDecisions.decision: Direct, slightly confrontational copy ('Most people selling you AI have never had to make payroll. I have.')
designDecisions.why: Owning two operating businesses while writing the software is Jay's real differentiator. Easy to soften in src/data/profile.ts if it ever needs to.

designDecisions.decision: A dossier stays open until dismissed, not until the ship drifts out of the sector
designDecisions.why: Auto-closing snatched content away mid-sentence. The ship also drops to 42% cruise speed while a dossier is open.

bugsFixedDuringRebuild: The #ui overlay won on CSS specificity and swallowed all pointer events, which silently killed drag-to-fly on touch devices.
The written brief lived inside a fixed full-viewport overlay, so the page could not scroll and in-page anchors went nowhere.
Dossiers closed themselves a few seconds after arrival as the ship drifted out of the sector radius.
The ORIGIN torus knot rendered as an invisible dark silhouette: a smooth knot has no hard edges, so EdgesGeometry produced nothing to draw.
Arriving at a sector whose node was already open advanced the run on the spot, so a returning visitor — or anyone replaying — flew the whole corridor end to end and was shown none of the resume.

The completion card matched none of its own stylesheet: `.finale__*` in the markup against `.done__*` in the CSS. No width cap, no padding, no background, no scroll, and every call to action off screen.

openItems.item: GitHub Pages is not automatic. Run `npm run deploy` and verify the mirror, or knotenvy.github.io/Knotz3DPortfolio serves the previous version from an indexed URL.

Two remote branches are fully contained in main and carry zero unmerged commits: claude/gamified-3d-portfolio-r7vfyi (the previous agent branch) and claude/3d-portfolio-polish-8dxhjx (this one). update-node-version is also fully merged but predates this work. Deleting them is lossless. This session could not do it — the git proxy returns HTTP 403 on a delete refspec and there is no API tool for it — so they need removing from the GitHub branches page.

The three items the final graphics review named, none of them defects. Boost still reads closer to fine speckle than to directional speed-lines — the streak strength and particle count both likely need another pass, not just the resize they got. The combat desaturation may be overcorrected: it solves legibility convincingly but the scene goes near-monochrome during fights, which is most of the runtime in a dense sector; keeping 10-15% more chroma in the floor grid would help. And per-sector prop silhouettes are genuinely different primitives now but read as similar at distance because they share a material treatment and clustering density.

Flagged independently by two reviewers in the final round: the player ship's engine glow is now the brightest element in frame, so the eye lands on your own ship before the hostiles — inverting the threats > ship > objective > scenery order the grading work was built around. Halving the ship's glow points fixed a blown-out silhouette but overshot for the engines. The clean fix is to let the engine glow ease down with the same combat dim the environment already uses (src/world/Environment.ts update), rather than another static number.

Reviewers rate the look as a well-executed take on a familiar neon idiom rather than something visually novel. Round-3 remediation closed the concrete defects — the nebula renders, the sky has parallax, threat markers read over bloom, panel lines carry at distance — so what is left here is art direction rather than bugs: a distinctive material or lighting idea, or a less trodden palette.
GameState (XP, ranks, achievement conditions) has no unit coverage. A mis-awarded achievement shipped and was caught by review rather than by a test.

A replay now stops at all six sectors, which is right, but it flies the full run-in to each one at cruise speed even though the visitor has already read everything — roughly four and a half minutes to re-reach UPLINK. The route spine and the pause panel's sector index both shortcut it, so nobody is trapped, but a shorter run-in for an already-decrypted sector would make a second pass feel deliberate rather than long.

Reviewers noted the six sectors run the same script six times — fly, fight, break the node, read the dossier — which is deliberate and good for conversion, but nothing escalates mechanically across sectors 2-6 the way the visuals imply it might.

The finale bug was a class-name rename that stopped halfway between the stylesheet and the markup, and nothing in the toolchain can see that: TypeScript does not check class strings and CSS does not know what the DOM emits. A build-time diff of the class names the TS emits against the ones the CSS defines would have caught it in a second. Worth adding if another component is ever renamed.

knownRisks: Both hosts must be republished together or they drift. Vercel redeploys automatically on push to main; GitHub Pages does not, and needs `npm run deploy`. If Pages is left stale it serves an old resume from an indexed URL.

Progress is stored in localStorage under the key `signal.save.v2`. Fields added since are filled in from defaults on load, so old saves still work; bumping the shape means bumping the version and the `v` check in src/core/Save.ts.
Custom ShaderMaterials do not receive three’s fog, lights or tone mapping automatically. Anything new that should sit in the same atmosphere has to implement fog itself, as src/shaders/hull.ts does.

Several bugs in this rebuild were of one shape: a factor in an alpha or intensity product silently going to zero, leaving an element rendering as nothing while looking correct in code. When something is invisible, check for a zeroed term before doubting the geometry.

#ui is a stack of fixed full-viewport layers over the canvas, and any one of them that takes pointer events becomes an invisible shield over everything beneath. base.css therefore lists which layers take pointers and defaults the rest to none. A new layer left off that list is visibly broken; a new layer wrongly added to it breaks everything under it silently. Three smoke checks assert the outcome.

Chromium interpolates a CSS transition or keyframe between a bare hex and a color-mix() through oklab(), and out-of-gamut midpoints can clip to a completely wrong hue — a violet objective card rendered a pure green ring for a whole animation. Both ends of any animated colour must be written with the same colour function.

Adding a uniform to a ShaderMaterial's uniforms object does not declare it in the GLSL. Miss the declaration and the shader fails to compile, the material draws nothing, and the game plays and reports identically — it looks like a tuning problem, not a broken shader. Check the console before tuning any effect that looks weak.

Emissive intensity is a deliberate hierarchy, not per-object taste: threats brightest (Enemy rim 2.4), then the ship (1.7), then the objective landmark (1.5), then scenery (0.62). Raising any one of them in isolation flattens the frame and the eye loses its focal point — reviewers reported exactly that when they were all near 1.0.

A dist/ mtime older than a commit does NOT mean the build is stale — the build runs before the commit. A reviewer inferred a stale-build process fault from exactly that and it was wrong. Verify what a bundle contains by grepping it or by measuring behaviour in the running app, never by comparing timestamps.

A CSS class rename is invisible to every check in this project. TypeScript does not type class strings, the CSS does not know what the DOM emits, and a behavioural test still passes because the elements are all present and clickable in the accessibility tree — the finale shipped unstyled for exactly this reason, on the one panel a visitor only reaches by finishing. When renaming a block, grep the other side.

`sector:decrypted` now carries `broken`. It is false when the ship simply flew back to a node that was already open, and anything that pays out — XP, the node count, the 'Unshaken' award, the detonation — must stay behind that flag or a visitor farms the same chapter by re-reading it.

conventions.codeStyle: Match the surrounding file. Comments explain why, not what. Strict TypeScript; the build fails on unused locals and parameters.

testing.philosophy: Not coverage. Every check is a bug that actually shipped and that a type-checker, a linter and a screenshot all failed to notice. Add to it the same way: when something breaks in a browser, write the check that would have caught it. Two further rules earned the hard way: a check that can pass without observing the state it describes is worse than no check, because it reports green — assert that the test did its work, not just that nothing went wrong. And behavioural checks cannot see a material that failed to build, so the console is part of the suite.

testing.note: The passive-visitor check is timing-marginal on a software renderer. In a swiftshader sandbox it took 268s of its 300s budget on the pre-change build and 172s after, and it does fail there on a slow run — it is measuring how long an autofiring ship takes to kill a node at 2-5 fps, not the product. On real hardware it finishes in seconds. If it fails, re-run before believing it, and compare against the previous build rather than weakening the check.
